chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever swears an oath and then sees what is better than it, let him do that which is better, and for him is a reward.

key_terms.حَسَنَة: Hasana — a good deed or divine reward; here indicating that breaking an oath for a better act is itself meritorious
key_terms.خَيْر: Khayr — goodness, the better option; the operative criterion for departing from an oath
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath (yameen) — a sworn commitment, legally binding in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they swear an oath but then find a better course of action?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) gives a ruling on the permissibility of breaking an oath when the oath-taker discovers a better course of action. Rather than holding rigidly to an oath that leads to a suboptimal outcome, Islam encourages choosing the better option, and the person who does so will even receive a divine reward. This teaching reflects the broader Islamic principle that divine law facilitates human welfare and does not bind believers to harmful or less beneficial commitments.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from one of our companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The one who swears an oath, so he sees what is better than it, so let him do that which is better, and for him would be a Reward’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from certain persons of our people who have narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one takes an oath to do something then finds another thing better which he does, he must do that which is better; he gains one good deed.’”
